claim: Acute kidney injury (AKI) has an incidence of around 34% in critically ill adults.
source: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is the most common cause of organ dysfunction in critically ill adults with an incidence of around 34% and carries an observed in-hospital mortality as high as 62% (Doyle and Forni, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Doyle and Forni, 2016.

claim: AKI carries an observed in-hospital mortality as high as 62%.
source: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is the most common cause of organ dysfunction in critically ill adults with an incidence of around 34% and carries an observed in-hospital mortality as high as 62% (Doyle and Forni, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Doyle and Forni, 2016.

claim: Mammals can partly repair their nephrons but cannot regenerate new ones.
source: One of the main reasons is that mammals can partly repair their nephrons (the functional units of the kidney), but cannot regenerate new ones.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Zebrafish can regenerate a large number of nephrons rapidly after kidney injury to compensate for lost renal function.
source: By contrast, zebrafish can regenerate a large number of nephrons rapidly after kidney injury to compensate for lost renal function (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Diep et al., 2011.

claim: During nephron regeneration, lhx1a-positive (lhx1a+) RPCs congregate to form cell aggregates.
source: During nephron regeneration, lhx1a-positive (lhx1a+) RPCs congregate to form cell aggregates, then proliferate rapidly and differentiate into renal vesicles (RVs), which finally develop into mature nephrons (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Diep et al., 2011.

claim: lhx1a+ RPCs proliferate rapidly after forming cell aggregates.
source: During nephron regeneration, lhx1a-positive (lhx1a+) RPCs congregate to form cell aggregates, then proliferate rapidly and differentiate into renal vesicles (RVs), which finally develop into mature nephrons (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Diep et al., 2011.

claim: lhx1a+ RPCs differentiate into renal vesicles (RVs).
source: During nephron regeneration, lhx1a-positive (lhx1a+) RPCs congregate to form cell aggregates, then proliferate rapidly and differentiate into renal vesicles (RVs), which finally develop into mature nephrons (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Diep et al., 2011.

claim: Renal vesicles (RVs) develop into mature nephrons.
source: During nephron regeneration, lhx1a-positive (lhx1a+) RPCs congregate to form cell aggregates, then proliferate rapidly and differentiate into renal vesicles (RVs), which finally develop into mature nephrons (Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Diep et al., 2011.

claim: The native microenvironment provides dynamic physical and chemical cues for progenitor and stem cell survival, proliferation, and function.
source: The native microenvironment in which progenitor and stem cells reside provides dynamic physical and chemical cues for their survival, proliferation, and function (Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2019.

claim: The types of cells that form the native microenvironment of RPCs have not been elucidated.
source: However, the types of cells that form the native microenvironment of RPCs have not been elucidated.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: RICs are specialized fibroblast-like cells localized mainly between the tubular and vascular structures.
source: RICs are specialized fibroblast-like cells localized mainly between the tubular and vascular structures, and thought to be responsible for the production of collagenous and noncollagenous extracellular matrices after kidney injury (Whiting et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Whiting et al., 1999.

claim: RICs are thought to be responsible for the production of collagenous and noncollagenous extracellular matrices after kidney injury.
source: RICs are specialized fibroblast-like cells localized mainly between the tubular and vascular structures, and thought to be responsible for the production of collagenous and noncollagenous extracellular matrices after kidney injury (Whiting et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Whiting et al., 1999.

claim: Under normal physiological conditions, RICs are the major sites of cyclooxygenase (Cox) expression and Cox-derived prostanoid synthesis.
source: Under normal physiological conditions, RICs are the major sites of cyclooxygenase (Cox) expression and Cox-derived prostanoid synthesis (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Prostanoids regulate various aspects of renal physiology, including tubular transport and hemodynamics.
source: Prostanoids regulate various aspects of renal physiology, including tubular transport and hemodynamics (Nasrallah et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nasrallah et al., 2007.

claim: RICs play diverse and crucial roles during renal development, homeostasis, and disease.
source: Numerous studies have reported the diverse and crucial roles of RICs during renal development, homeostasis, and disease (Whiting et al., 1999; Nasrallah et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Whiting et al., 1999; Nasrallah et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: The roles of RICs during nephron regeneration remain undefined.
source: However, the roles of RICs during nephron regeneration remain undefined.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: PGE2 is one of the most typical lipid mediators produced from arachidonic acid (AA) by Cox enzymes.
source: PGE2 is one of the most typical lipid mediators produced from arachidonic acid (AA) by Cox enzymes (Park et al., 2006) and has been demonstrated to play a crucial role in the development of pronephros (Chambers et al., 2020; Marra et al., 2019; Poureetezadi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Park et al., 2006.

claim: PGE2 has been demonstrated to play a crucial role in the development of pronephros.
source: PGE2 is one of the most typical lipid mediators produced from arachidonic acid (AA) by Cox enzymes (Park et al., 2006) and has been demonstrated to play a crucial role in the development of pronephros (Chambers et al., 2020; Marra et al., 2019; Poureetezadi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chambers et al., 2020; Marra et al., 2019; Poureetezadi et al., 2016.

claim: Elevation of PGE2 can restrict the formation of the distal nephron segment and expand a proximal segment lineage in zebrafish.
source: Elevation of PGE2 can restrict the formation of the distal nephron segment and expand a proximal segment lineage in zebrafish (Poureetezadi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Poureetezadi et al., 2016.

claim: PGE2 regulates the development of renal multicilliated cells.
source: PGE2 also regulates the development of renal multicilliated cells, in which embryos deficient in PGE2 form fewer renal multiciliated cell progenitors and develop more transporter cells (Marra et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Marra et al., 2019.

claim: Embryos deficient in PGE2 form fewer renal multiciliated cell progenitors and develop more transporter cells.
source: PGE2 also regulates the development of renal multicilliated cells, in which embryos deficient in PGE2 form fewer renal multiciliated cell progenitors and develop more transporter cells (Marra et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Marra et al., 2019.

claim: Whether PGE2 affects nephrogenesis during regeneration of the zebrafish mesonephros has not been investigated.
source: However, whether PGE2 affects nephrogenesis during regeneration of the zebrafish mesonephros has not been investigated.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Single-cell sequencing of zebrafish kidney revealed that fabp10a is a marker of RICs.
source: In this study, we have employed single-cell sequencing in zebrafish kidney and have revealed that fabp10a is a marker of RICs.
evidence: The claim is based on data from single-cell sequencing performed in this study.

claim: RICs can be specifically labeled by GFP in the fabp10a:GFP transgenic kidney.
source: RICs can be specifically labeled by GFP in the fabp10a:GFP transgenic kidney.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations using the transgenic line.

claim: The formation of nephrons is closely related to Cox2a-expressed RICs, which are in close contact with RPC aggregates during nephron regeneration.
source: The formation of nephrons is closely related to Cox2a-expressed RICs, which are in close contact with RPC aggregates during nephron regeneration.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations in this study.

claim: Inhibiting PGE2 production suppresses nephrogenesis.
source: Inhibiting PGE2 production suppresses nephrogenesis.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from inhibitor studies.

claim: PGE2 interacts with the Wnt signaling pathway by regulating β-catenin stability in RPC aggregates.
source: Furthermore, PGE2 interacts with the Wnt signaling pathway by regulating β-catenin stability in RPC aggregates and can rescue the nephron regeneration defect in wnt4a mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from this study.

claim: PGE2 can rescue the nephron regeneration defect in wnt4a mutants.
source: Furthermore, PGE2 interacts with the Wnt signaling pathway by regulating β-catenin stability in RPC aggregates and can rescue the nephron regeneration defect in wnt4a mutants.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from this study.

claim: RICs secrete PGE2 to promote nephron regeneration by PGE2/Wnt interaction.
source: These findings illustrate that RICs secrete PGE2 to promote nephron regeneration by PGE2/Wnt interaction.
evidence: The claim is based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: Six randomly selected 6-month-old zebrafish kidneys were used to obtain about 7147 cells for sequencing.
source: Six randomly selected 6-month-old zebrafish kidneys were used to obtain about 7147 cells for sequencing.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the study.

claim: 3902 cells passed the quality control and were incorporated into analyses.
source: 3902 cells passed the quality control and were incorporated into analyses.
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the study.

claim: The initial analysis of kidney samples identified distinct clusters comprising 12 different cell types.
source: Our initial analysis of kidney samples identified distinct clusters comprising 12 different cell types (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on data analysis shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Distal tubule epithelial cells are defined by expression of solute carrier family 12 member 3 (slc12a3), ATPase Na+/K+ transporting subunit alpha 1a, tandem duplicate 4 (atp1a1a.4), and ATPase Na+/K+ transporting subunit beta 1a (atp1b1a).
source: For example, two cell clusters were composed of epithelial cell types that are highly conserved in mammals, including the distal tubule epithelial cells defined by expression of solute carrier family 12 member 3 (slc12a3), ATPase Na+/K+ transporting subunit alpha 1a, tandem duplicate 4 (atp1a1a.4), and ATPase Na+/K+ transporting subunit beta 1a (atp1b1a), as well as the proximal tubule epithelial cells defined by the expression of solute carrier family 22 member 2 (slc22a2), paired box 2a (pax2a), and aminoacylase 1 (acy1) (Tang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on gene expression data and supported by a citation to Tang et al., 2017.

claim: Proximal tubule epithelial cells are defined by the expression of solute carrier family 22 member 2 (slc22a2), paired box 2a (pax2a), and aminoacylase 1 (acy1).
source: For example, two cell clusters were composed of epithelial cell types that are highly conserved in mammals, including the distal tubule epithelial cells defined by expression of solute carrier family 12 member 3 (slc12a3), ATPase Na+/K+ transporting subunit alpha 1a, tandem duplicate 4 (atp1a1a.4), and ATPase Na+/K+ transporting subunit beta 1a (atp1b1a), as well as the proximal tubule epithelial cells defined by the expression of solute carrier family 22 member 2 (slc22a2), paired box 2a (pax2a), and aminoacylase 1 (acy1) (Tang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on gene expression data and supported by a citation to Tang et al., 2017.

claim: Cluster 12 expressed human or mouse RICs signature genes, including collagen type 1 alpha 1b (col1a1b), collagen type 1 alpha 2 (col1a2), decorin (dcn), and elastin microfibril interfacer 1a (emilin1a).
source: By comparing our data with the single-cell RNA sequencing data of human and mouse kidneys, it was found that this cluster of cells expressed human or mouse RICs signature genes, including collagen type 1 alpha 1b (col1a1b), collagen type 1 alpha 2 (col1a2), decorin (dcn), and elastin microfibril interfacer 1a (emilin1a) (Young et al., 2018; Stewart et al., 2019; Ransick et al., 2019; Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is based on gene expression data and comparison with published data, supported by citations to Young et al., 2018; Stewart et al., 2019; Ransick et al., 2019.

claim: GO analysis of cluster 12 showed that a significant percentage of genes corresponded to the extracellular matrix.
source: We next performed gene ontology (GO) analysis of all genes in this cell cluster and found that a significant percentage of genes corresponded to the extracellular matrix, the extracellular proteins that are not attached to the cell surface, or response to steroid hormones.
evidence: The claim is based on GO analysis performed in this study.

claim: Cluster 12 was enriched in genes that respond to lipids.
source: Furthermore, this cluster of cells was also enriched in genes that respond to lipids (Figure 1C), which are richly contained by mammalian RICs (Hao and Breyer, 2007).
evidence: The claim is based on GO analysis shown in Figure 1C and supported by a citation to Hao and Breyer, 2007.

claim: Fatty acid-binding protein 10a (fabp10a) was specifically expressed in cell cluster 12 but not in other type cells.
source: Notably, we found that fatty acid-binding protein 10a (fabp10a), which plays a pivotal role in intracellular binding and trafficking of long-chain fatty acids (Her et al., 2003), was specifically expressed in cell cluster 12 but not in other type cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on gene expression data shown in Figure 1D and supported by a citation to Her et al., 2003.

claim: Tg(fabp10a:GFP) has been reported to specifically label the liver during early embryonic development.
source: Tg(fabp10a:GFP) has been reported to specifically label the liver during early embryonic development (Her et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Her et al., 2003.

claim: Tg(fabp10a:GFP) labeled not only the liver and spinal cord but also a part of proximal straight tubule (PST) and distal tubule (DT) starting at 4 days post-fertilization (4 dpf).
source: To observe the expression of fabp10a in the kidney, we crossed Tg(fabp10a:GFP) with Tg(cdh17:DsRed), which is a transgenic line specifically labeled nephron epithelial cells, and found that Tg(fabp10a:GFP) labeled not only the liver and spinal cord but also a part of proximal straight tubule (PST) and distal tubule (DT) starting at 4 days post-fertilization (4 dpf) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A large number of Tg(fabp10a:GFP) labeled cells were observed to distribute around the area where the mesonephric tubules appeared after 15 dpf.
source: Furthermore, a large number of Tg(fabp10a:GFP) labeled cells were observed to distribute around the area where the mesonephric tubules appeared after 15 dpf (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Tg(fabp10a:GFP) labeled cells were fusiform with irregular polygon shapes, and interweaved between cells to form a network.
source: These cells were fusiform with irregular polygon shapes, and interweaved between cells to form a network (Figure 2A), similar to the same cell shape as mammalian RICs (Whiting et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 2A and supported by citations to Whiting et al., 1999; Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: GFP+ cells were attached to the renal tubules and collecting ducts, or distributed in the renal interstitium in adult kidney sections.
source: To further identify these cells, we analyzed adult kidney sections of the Tg(fapb10a:GFP;cdh17:DsRed) double transgenic line. A large number of GFP+ cells were attached to the renal tubules and collecting ducts, or distributed in the renal interstitium (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GFP+ cells tightly surrounded the cdh17-labeled renal capsules.
source: Moreover, these cells also tightly surrounded the cdh17-labeled renal capsules (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 2C.

claim: fabp10a expression was detected in GFP+/DsRed- cells but not in control cells by semi-quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).
source: We detected the fabp10a expression in GFP+/DsRed- cells but not in control cells by semi-quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating that GFP+/DsRed- cells were indeed fabp10a positive.
evidence: The claim is based on RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Erythropoietin (epo) gene was enriched in GFP+/DsRed- cells, but not in control cells.
source: Furthermore, we detected the enrichment of erythropoietin (epo) gene, a marker of mammalian RICs (Kobayashi et al., 2016; Souma et al., 2015), in GFP +/DsRed- cells, but not in control cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2D and supported by citations to Kobayashi et al., 2016; Souma et al., 2015.

claim: cox2a was highly enriched in GFP+/DsRed- cells.
source: Cox2 is also considered to be a marker of mammalian RICs (Zhang et al., 2018). We found that cox2a, the Cox2-orthologous gene in zebrafish, was also highly enriched in GFP+/DsRed- cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2D and supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: RICs have been reported to differentiate into fibroblasts when AKI occurs in mammals.
source: RICs have been reported to differentiate into fibroblasts when AKI occurs in mammals (Baues et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Baues et al., 2020.

claim: mRNA levels of fibroblast markers col1a1b and col1a2 were increased significantly in GFP+/DsRed- cells at 5 dpi compared with the uninjured kidneys.
source: Compared with the uninjured kidneys, mRNA levels of fibroblast markers col1a1b and col1a2 were increased significantly in GFP+/DsRed- cells at 5 dpi according to quantitative PCR (qPCR) analysis (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: The claim is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: Many lipid droplets were detected in the cytoplasm of most Tg(fabp10a:GFP) labeled cells.
source: Because mammalian RICs are lipid-rich cells (Hao and Breyer, 2007), Nile red, a fluorescent dye that specifically stains lipids, was used to detect lipid droplets in adult renal tissues. Many lipid droplets were detected in the cytoplasm of most Tg(fabp10a:GFP) labeled cells (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: The claim is based on Nile red staining data shown in Figure 2G and H and supported by a citation to Hao and Breyer, 2007.

claim: Kidney injury in adult zebrafish induces the synchronous formation of many new nephrons marked by lhx1a.
source: Kidney injury in adult zebrafish induces the synchronous formation of many new nephrons marked by lhx1a (Kamei et al., 2019; Diep et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kamei et al., 2019; Diep et al., 2011.

claim: The lhx1a+ RPC aggregates were wrapped around by the RICs that closely interacted with lhx1a+ cells in injured kidneys.
source: In the Tg(fapb10a:GFP;lhx1a:DsRed) injured kidneys, we found that the lhx1a + RPC aggregates were wrapped around by the RICs that closely interacted with lhx1a + cells (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RICs and lhx1a+ RPCs proliferated simultaneously after AKI.
source: Additionally, EdU assay showed that RICs and lhx1a + RPCs proliferated simultaneously after AKI (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that RICs participate in the regeneration of nephrons.
evidence: The claim is based on EdU assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: RICs participate in the regeneration of nephrons.
source: Additionally, EdU assay showed that RICs and lhx1a + RPCs proliferated simultaneously after AKI (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that RICs participate in the regeneration of nephrons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that RICs and RPCs proliferate simultaneously.

claim: During the development of mesonephros from 10 dpf to 16 dpf, RPCs occurred with the pronephric tubules at the 4.6 mm stage.
source: During the development of mesonephros from 10 dpf to 16 dpf, RPCs occurred with the pronephric tubules at the 4.6 mm stage (body length; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) and RICs were detected around the RPC at the 5 mm stage.
evidence: The claim is based on time-lapse microscopy observations shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: RICs were detected around the RPC at the 5 mm stage.
source: During the development of mesonephros from 10 dpf to 16 dpf, RPCs occurred with the pronephric tubules at the 4.6 mm stage (body length; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A) and RICs were detected around the RPC at the 5 mm stage.
evidence: The claim is based on time-lapse microscopy observations.

claim: RPCs congregate to form the first cell aggregate at the 5 mm stage.
source: At this time, the RPCs congregate to form the first cell aggregate (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and D).
evidence: The claim is based on time-lapse microscopy observations shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and D.

claim: The RPC aggregate elongated to form the first mesonephric branch at the 5.3 mm stage.
source: The RPC aggregate then elongated to form the first mesonephric branch at the 5.3 mm stage, and large numbers of RICs appeared in the direction of elongation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and E).
evidence: The claim is based on time-lapse microscopy observations shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and E.

claim: The mesonephric tubule elongated and formed the nascent nephron at the 5.8 mm stage.
source: Further, the mesonephric tubule elongated and formed the nascent nephron at the 5.8 mm stage, and RICs formed a network that completely wrapped the entire nephron (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F, Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: The claim is based on time-lapse microscopy observations shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F.

claim: RICs formed a network that completely wrapped the entire nephron at the 5.8 mm stage.
source: Further, the mesonephric tubule elongated and formed the nascent nephron at the 5.8 mm stage, and RICs formed a network that completely wrapped the entire nephron (Figure 3—figure supplement 2F, Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: The claim is based on time-lapse microscopy observations shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2F.

claim: The RIC network is a basic element of nephron structure.
source: This finding demonstrates that the RIC network is a basic element of nephron structure.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that RICs wrap nephrons during development.

claim: A large number of RICs were EdU+ during nephrogenesis.
source: Furthermore, we also determined the proliferation of RICs during this process, and found a large number of RICs were EdU+, as in regeneration stage (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G), indicating that cell proliferation during nephrogenesis is a source of RICs.
evidence: The claim is based on EdU assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2G.

claim: Cell proliferation during nephrogenesis is a source of RICs.
source: Furthermore, we also determined the proliferation of RICs during this process, and found a large number of RICs were EdU+, as in regeneration stage (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G), indicating that cell proliferation during nephrogenesis is a source of RICs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that RICs are proliferating during nephrogenesis.

claim: RICs are closely related to nephrogenesis.
source: The above results indicate that RICs are closely related to nephrogenesis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observations of RIC behavior during nephrogenesis.

claim: The expression of cox2a was increased significantly after AKI compared to uninjured tissues according to transcriptome data.
source: In order to analyze the molecular mechanism of nephron regeneration, we performed the renal transcriptome analyses using injured kidney tissues at 1, 3, 5, and 7 dpi (Figure 3—source data 1). The transcriptome data showed that the expression of cox2a, a marker gene of RICs, was increased significantly after AKI compared to uninjured tissues.
evidence: The claim is based on transcriptome data from this study.

claim: cox2a mRNA expression increased at 1 dpi, reached its highest level at 5 dpi, and returned to normal at 9 dpi.
source: Further, we confirmed this result by RT-PCR and found that cox2a mRNA expression increased at 1 dpi, reached its highest level at 5 dpi, and returned to normal at 9 dpi (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is based on RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Cox2a was increased during nephron regeneration according to immunofluorescence.
source: Furthermore, immunofluorescence revealed that Cox2a was increased during nephron regeneration (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Most of the Cox2a-positive RICs were in close contact with RPC aggregates.
source: Interestingly, most of the Cox2a-positive RICs were in close contact with RPC aggregates (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is based on immunofluorescence observations shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Cox2 is a rate-limiting enzyme in PGE2 synthesis.
source: Cox2 is a rate-limiting enzyme in PGE2 synthesis (Nørregaard et al., 2015; Poureetezadi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Nørregaard et al., 2015; Poureetezadi et al., 2016.

claim: PGE2 levels were about 69.7% higher in injured groups than uninjured control groups at 1 dpi.
source: We examined PGE2 levels in kidneys using immunosorbent (ELISA) assay and found that PGE2 was increased significantly during nephron regeneration. The PGE2 levels were about 69.7% higher in injured groups than uninjured control groups at 1 dpi and reached their maximum value at 5 dpi (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is based on ELISA data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PGE2 levels reached their maximum value at 5 dpi.
source: We examined PGE2 levels in kidneys using immunosorbent (ELISA) assay and found that PGE2 was increased significantly during nephron regeneration. The PGE2 levels were about 69.7% higher in injured groups than uninjured control groups at 1 dpi and reached their maximum value at 5 dpi (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is based on ELISA data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The expression of cox2a was increased during nephron regeneration according to qPCR.
source: We next evaluated the expression of cox1, cox2a, and cox2b, the zebrafish cox gene family, by qPCR. The results showed that the expression of cox2a was increased (Figure 3A), whereas cox2b expression was reduced during nephron regeneration.
evidence: The claim is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: cox2b expression was reduced during nephron regeneration.
source: We next evaluated the expression of cox1, cox2a, and cox2b, the zebrafish cox gene family, by qPCR. The results showed that the expression of cox2a was increased (Figure 3A), whereas cox2b expression was reduced during nephron regeneration.
evidence: The claim is based on qPCR data.

claim: cox1 expression remained unaltered during nephron regeneration.
source: However, cox1 expression remained unaltered (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: The claim is based on qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: AKI could induce RICs to specifically express cox2a that increases the synthesis and secretion of PGE2.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that AKI could induce RICs to specifically express cox2a that increases the synthesis and secretion of PGE2.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observations of cox2a expression and PGE2 levels after AKI.

claim: Suppressing Cox activity with indomethacin restrains nephron regeneration.
source: To assess whether endogenous PGE2 participates in nephron regeneration after AKI, we intraperitoneally injected indomethacin (Indo, 200 μM, 10 μL per fish), an inhibitor of both Cox1 and Cox2, at 2, 4, and 6 dpi (Poureetezadi et al., 2016). Whole-mount in situ hybridization (WISH) showed that the number of lhx1a+ cell aggregates was decreased at 7 dpi compared with the control group (Figure 3D, G–I, P). lhx1a expression was also reduced (Figure 3D). These results indicate that suppressing Cox activity restrains nephron regeneration.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 3D, G–I, P and supported by a citation to Poureetezadi et al., 2016.

claim: NS-398, a selective Cox2 inhibitor, decreased lhx1a expression and the number of lhx1a+ cell aggregates.
source: To test this, N-(2-cyclohexyloxy-4-nitrophenyl) methane sulfonamide (NS-398, 140 μM, 10 μL per fish), a selective Cox2 inhibitor (Marra et al., 2019), was injected after AKI. As a result, lhx1a expression and the number of lhx1a+ cell aggregates was decreased, as in the Indo-treated group (Figure 3D, J and P).
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data from inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 3D, J and P and supported by a citation to Marra et al., 2019.

claim: There were no obvious morphological differences between cox2a-/- and wild-type (WT) sibling fish.
source: To further explore these findings, we used a genetic model of Cox2a deficiency to assess the effects of the Cox2a-PGE2 pathway on nephron regeneration. There were no obvious morphological differences between cox2a-/- and wild-type (WT) sibling fish (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is based on observations and supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: lhx1a mRNA and the number of lhx1a+ cell aggregates in cox2a-/- kidneys were less than injured WT kidneys at 7 dpi.
source: We next induced AKI in cox2a-/- mutants and found that lhx1a mRNA and the number of lhx1a+ cell aggregates in cox2a-/- kidneys were less than injured WT kidneys at 7 dpi (Figure 3E, K and P), indicating that Cox2a is required for nephron regeneration.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3E, K and P.

claim: Cox2a is required for nephron regeneration.
source: We next induced AKI in cox2a-/- mutants and found that lhx1a mRNA and the number of lhx1a+ cell aggregates in cox2a-/- kidneys were less than injured WT kidneys at 7 dpi (Figure 3E, K and P), indicating that Cox2a is required for nephron regeneration.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that cox2a-/- mutants have reduced nephron regeneration.

claim: PGE2 level in cox2a-/- kidneys at 5 dpi was significantly lower than that in injured WT kidneys.
source: We next measured PGE2 level in cox2a-/- kidneys at 5 dpi and found it was significantly lower than that in injured WT kidneys, while no significant differences were detectable between uninjured cox2a-/- and WT groups (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is based on ELISA data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.
